title: Honest work
hook: Guru Nanak squeezed two meals, and one bled: the Sikh, Muslim and Buddhist teachings on honest earning
tomorrow: a monk lay sick and alone. who finally came to wash him?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: the other handle. Plato froze with his hand in the air. Today, a quieter test at work, the kind nobody checks.

Rounding up a timesheet. Calling a stock photo your own. Small things, and nobody checks. Sikh tradition tells a story about exactly that. Guru Nanak, the story goes, stayed in a town with Lalo, a carpenter who lived on coarse bread he earned with his own hands. A rich official, Malik Bhago, threw a feast and demanded the Guru come. He came. Then he took Lalo's dry bread in one hand and Bhago's rich food in the other, and squeezed. From Lalo's bread, milk. From Bhago's feast, blood. So why would bread bleed?
screen: `A TIMESHEET NOBODY CHECKS.` → `LALO'S BREAD, BHAGO'S FEAST.` → `MILK FROM ONE, BLOOD FROM THE OTHER.`

segments.voice: Because, the story says, Bhago's wealth had been squeezed out of the poor. The food carried how it was earned. The story comes from the janamsakhis, the life stories Sikhs tell of Guru Nanak, and it sits behind a plain Sikh teaching: kirat karni, earning by honest work. In the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Nanak says that the one who eats what he earns by his own effort, and gives some of it away, is the one who recognizes the path. Sikh teaching sets it beside two others: remember God, and share what you have. Two neighbor traditions say it in their own words. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari has the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, saying that no one eats better food than what he eats from the work of his own hands. And the Buddha's eightfold path includes right livelihood: earning in a way that does no harm. Three traditions, each with its own reasons. The puzzle's answer isn't a magic trick. It's a question about a paycheck: what got squeezed into it? Lalo's bread wasn't holy because it was plain. It was clean because nothing in it was taken: not someone else's time, not their credit, not their sweat.
screen: `WEALTH SQUEEZED OUT OF THE POOR.` · `KIRAT KARNI: EARN BY HONEST WORK.` · `FROM THE WORK OF HIS OWN HANDS.` · `RIGHT LIVELIHOOD: EARN WITHOUT HARM.` · then, large: `HONEST.`

segments.voice: Pick up one thing your work paid for: your phone, your lunch, the cup in front of you. Hold it, and ask Lalo's question quietly: how was this earned? If one part of your work wouldn't survive being squeezed, just name it to yourself, and keep breathing.
Honest work: earning by your own effort, so the bread holds milk, not blood. Sikhs call it kirat karni.
Pocket this one: honest, like Lalo's bread, coarse and clean all the way through. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1710 COUNTS.` → `AT WORK · 4 OF 7.` → `TOMORROW: A MONK LAY SICK AND ALONE. WHO FINALLY CAME TO WASH HIM?`

howItsDone: Sikhs speak of kirat karni, earning by honest work, alongside remembering God and sharing; Muslims and Buddhists have their own teachings on honest earning and right livelihood.
